scope: native_products hook counters and MIR scope timers describe the first hooked attempt only; after fresh_context_fallbacks, subsequent ordinary native work has unavailable per-pass counts. Reuse in a discarded attempt is not work avoided by final compilation. Native receipt phase/total times and request wall include the full native fallback; request wall also includes all driver retries. MIR timers are scopes, not a partition of native total. In typed-body sources, mir_parse_ns includes tiny-header parsing, current typed MI/MBB/use-chain construction and parser/header destruction; it is not pure YAML parsing. mir_restore_validate_ns includes target/number/block state, typed recapture equality, domain, MachineVerifier and full MIR equality. Compare timer definitions at each pinned compiler source. Observer v3 IR scopes: key is supported-entry eligibility/current facts/Input/World/pipeline; unpack is complete selected-slot decode; replay includes parse/clone/current validation/AM/cleanup; parse is only MemoryBuffer+parseBitcodeFile construction, excluding later Module destruction, and is already INCLUDED in replay. Capture is the complete afterStage callback, including cheap early-return gates and new-stage packing. Pack is new-stage admission/frame/SHA/zstd/typed metadata/publication and is already INCLUDED in capture. Do not add child timers to parents, call these a partition, or classify original unknown FPM passes as measured overhead. Observer v1/v2 IR scopes are unavailable (None), not zero. Clock overhead stays in request wall.
limits: All preparation and measured rows retained. Diagnostic only; no cross-window ratio, causal attribution or formal acceptance. Retained bytes are a per-request receipt sum, not peak RSS or a lifetime bound.
